edges.reason: _msgSender() returns the untrusted msg.sender, which becomes the identity used for all authorization.
Ownable constructor reads _msgSender() to set the privileged _owner.
Constructor writes the derived sender into state variable _owner.
onlyOwner reads _owner when enforcing the authorization check.
Untrusted msg.sender is compared against _owner inside onlyOwner.
onlyOwner modifier gates execution of renounceOwnership.
renounceOwnership writes address(0) into _owner, permanently dropping privileges.
generate() is guarded by the onlyOwner modifier.
Caller identity reaches generate() through the onlyOwner modifier check.
Caller-supplied length parameter is consumed by generate().
length is an operand of the unbounded currentIndex + length addition.
currentIndex is an operand of the currentIndex + length addition.
Result of the addition, clamped by the ternary, determines endIndex.
length participates in computing endIndex either directly or via the sum.
endIndex is written back to currentIndex at the end of generate().
block.timestamp is fed into the randomness seed, making output miner/timestamp dependent.
Randomness parity decides whether an index is pushed into the stud array.
Randomness parity decides whether an index is pushed into the dam array.
Loop counter i is one of the hashed inputs of the randomness derivation.
keccak256 hashOfRandom is converted to numberRepresentation.
numberRepresentation % 2 selects the branch that mutates stud/dam state.
currentIndex is read as the loop start and compared against 10000 in generate().
StudList exposes the stud state array.
DamList exposes the dam state array.
Local msgSender variable holds the caller identity used to initialize _owner.

normalization_plan.reason: length is only consumed by generate(); it should be folded into the function's input signature rather than modelled as a standalone node.
endIndex is a purely internal loop bound of generate() with no independent security meaning.
Loop counter i is only used as a hashed input feeding the randomness derivation.
hashOfRandom exists only as an intermediate value of the keccak256 randomness computation.
numberRepresentation is a transient cast of the hash whose parity drives the stud/dam push.
msgSender is a short-lived temporary inside the Ownable constructor used to set _owner.
